concepts.title: Cell Size Estimation
concepts.definition: The actual size of a microscopic specimen can be determined by dividing the diameter of the microscope's field of view by the number of cells spanning that diameter.
concepts.key_idea: Microscopic dimensions are calculated by relating the field of view to the number of cells observed across it.
question_patterns: calculate the size of a cell
estimate the real size of a cell
what is the dimension of a cell if field diameter is ...
find the cell size given cell count
calculate cell size estimation for the given values

solution_steps.action: Identify the field diameter and cell count
solution_steps.explain: Read the microscope's field of view diameter in micrometers and count how many cells span that diameter.
Divide the total field diameter in micrometers by the number of cells counted along that diameter.

solution_steps.action: Express the result in appropriate units
solution_steps.explain: The computed value is in micrometers; confirm it falls within a biologically plausible range for the cell type being observed.

concepts.title: Microscope Magnification
concepts.definition: Total magnification is the magnifying power of the eyepiece multiplied by that of the objective lens.
concepts.key_idea: Total magnification is the combined magnifying effect of the ocular and objective lenses.
question_patterns: what is the total magnification
calculate total magnification given lens powers

solution_steps.action: Identify eyepiece and objective lens powers
solution_steps.explain: Read the magnifying power engraved on the eyepiece (ocular) lens and the objective lens currently in use.
Multiply the magnifying power of the eyepiece by the magnifying power of the objective lens.
Check that the result falls within the expected range for a compound microscope (typically 10x to 2000x).

concepts.title: Cell Membrane Permeability
concepts.definition: The cell membrane acts as a selective barrier, regulating the movement of materials like water, salts, and gases into and out of the cell.
concepts.key_idea: Selectively permeable membranes allow specific molecules to pass while restricting others, driving processes like osmosis.
question_patterns: explain the role of the cell membrane
what is selective permeability
how do substances move across the membrane
describe the function of the plasma membrane
what do you understand by cell membrane permeability

solution_steps.explain: The cell membrane controls internal environment by allowing selective passage of solutes and solvents.
The lipid bilayer allows small non-polar molecules to diffuse freely while transport proteins regulate the passage of ions and larger polar molecules.

solution_steps.action: Relate permeability to osmosis and material transport
solution_steps.explain: Selective permeability drives osmosis -- water moves across the membrane from a region of lower solute concentration to higher solute concentration until equilibrium is reached.

concepts.title: Cell Division Types
concepts.definition: Mitosis forms two genetically matching daughter cells for growth and repair, while meiosis produces four genetically diverse gametes with half the chromosome count for sexual reproduction.
concepts.key_idea: Mitosis maintains genetic consistency, whereas meiosis introduces variation and reduces chromosome number.
question_patterns: differentiate between mitosis and meiosis
what is the outcome of mitosis
how does meiosis differ from mitosis
compare the daughter cells of mitosis and meiosis
list the main features of cell division types

solution_steps.explain: Mitosis results in identical somatic cells; meiosis results in specialized reproductive cells with reduced chromosome sets.

solution_steps.action: Compare daughter cell counts and ploidy
solution_steps.explain: Mitosis produces two daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the parent (diploid), while meiosis produces four daughter cells with half the chromosome number (haploid).

solution_steps.action: Relate each division type to its biological purpose
solution_steps.explain: Mitosis supports growth, tissue repair, and asexual reproduction by maintaining genetic consistency; meiosis enables sexual reproduction by introducing genetic variation through crossing over and independent assortment.
